summary: This bill amends the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act to add alpha-gal (galactose-alpha-1,3-galactose, including certain mammal-derived ingredients and red algae) to the definition of major food allergen, with the change taking effect 18 months after enactment.

scores.thoughts: The bill amends the definition of major food allergens under the FD&C Act to include alpha-gal. It contains no provisions related to federal spending, appropriations, or budget authority.
The bill makes no changes to tax law, rates, deductions, or revenue collection.

While alpha-gal syndrome is a medical condition, the bill addresses only food labeling requirements and does not alter healthcare coverage, delivery systems, insurance, or public vs. private healthcare structures.
No provisions relate to firearms, regulations, or Second Amendment issues.
The bill has no connection to immigration policy, visas, borders, or enforcement.
No provisions address reproductive rights or abortion access.
No references to military, defense budgets, or national security spending.
Mentions of red algae are solely for allergen definition purposes; the bill does not create or modify environmental regulations or protections.
No provisions affect welfare programs, SNAP, or other safety-net benefits.
The bill does not address schools, education funding, or school choice.
No provisions relate to controlled substances, decriminalization, or drug enforcement.
No provisions address sentencing, policing, or criminal justice reform.
The bill does not impose tariffs, trade barriers, or alter trade agreements.
No fiscal provisions affecting deficits or debt reduction.
No provisions address LGBTQ+ legal protections or rights.
No provisions relate to foreign assistance or international aid.
No provisions address voting rights, election procedures, or voter ID.
No provisions address technology regulation, data privacy, or surveillance.
No provisions affect labor law, unions, or worker/employer relations.
No provisions address religious exemptions or anti-discrimination laws.
